about: A single-size, Cuban-style blend made by the Serino family with David Imber, using five-year-old tobaccos and traditional methods such as slow fermentation, wooden molds and hand bunching. It is rolled at La Corona in Estelí and sold in 10-count boxes.

about: Serino's value-priced line, first rolled for a family friend's destination wedding and later turned into a regular release. It is made at La Corona in Estelí and sold in paper-wrapped bundles of 10 with a pigtail cap and brushed foot.

about: A limited 9 1/4 inch A-size cigar from Serino built around tobaccos from the 2012 crop, rolled at La Corona in 2016 and then aged before release. It was sold in single coffins.
notes: Limited to 1,000 single coffins. halfwheel found it mild to mild-medium; Developing Palates called it medium. Ring gauge is 47 in the spec tables, though halfwheel's text also says 49.
